\begin{abstract}
Payment Delegation (benchmark-payment-delegation) is a public npm benchmark package in the benchmark-* family, version 0.1.0, status alpha. This report records what the package measures in its own words, its deterministic grader and its SDK, CLI, MCP and HTTP surfaces, and the offline validation the family data holds: a scripted good policy mean of 1 and a scripted bad policy mean of 0 over 40 tasks, from mock runs at seeds 1 and 2 on the public task split generated with seed 20261015. The review record shows 3 fix rounds, 1 defect classes with public locators, and 9 merged feature pull requests of which 6 were approved. It was not part of the preregistered trivial-policy check. No real-model scores are reported. Software concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23422414, family paper DOI 10.5281/zenodo.23428802.
\end{abstract}
\section{What the package asks}
The package states its question in its own README:
% quote: benchmark-payment-delegation/README.md#L7
\begin{quote}
benchmark-payment-delegation measures whether an agent with a
delegated card respects spending caps, merchant allowlists, refund
windows, and dispute policy while completing purchase goals. Companion
to
\href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-checkout-consent}{benchm\allowbreak 
ark-checkout-consent} (explicit checkout consent); this repo focuses
on ledger policy, not the consent moment.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-payment-delegation/blob/v0.1.0/README.md#L7}{\texttt{benchmark-payment-delegation:README.md\#L7}}.}

Its index entry states the measured construct as: ``Whether an agent respects spending caps, merchant allowlists, refund rules, and dispute policy when given a delegated card.'' (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, \texttt{benchmark-payment-delegation.whatItMeasures}).

\section{Offline validation}
No real model was run. The family data records mock runs at seeds \pkgMockSeedA{} and \pkgMockSeedB{}
over the public task split generated with seed \pkgPublicSeed{}, on version \pkgVersion{}:
the scripted good policy reaches a mean of \pkgGoodMean{} (weakest task \pkgGoodMin{}),
the scripted bad policy a mean of \pkgBadMean{} (best task \pkgBadMax{}),
and the run at mock seed \pkgMockSeedA{} scores \pkgMockMean{} over \pkgTaskCount{} tasks
with a bootstrap interval of \pkgMockCiLow{} to \pkgMockCiHigh{} (\pkgMockPassed{} tasks passed; cost \$\pkgMockCost{}).
Source: \texttt{paper/data/suite.json}, collected by \texttt{scripts/collect.mjs}.
The README prints a sample run:
% quote: benchmark-payment-delegation/README.md#L14
\begin{quote}\ttfamily
\#~Payment~Delegation\\
-~Model:~\textasciigrave{}mock:1\textasciigrave{}\\
-~Score:~**57.5\%**\\
-~Tasks:~40\\
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-payment-delegation/blob/v0.1.0/README.md#L14}{\texttt{benchmark-payment-delegation:README.md\#L14}}.}

\section{Preregistered trivial-policy check}
The check design is described in the family paper: trivial policies ran each package in the registered set
at \pkgTrivialVerOld{} and \pkgTrivialVerNew{} through a local fake model server answering through
the package's own OpenAI provider (\texttt{paper/sections/prereg.tex}).
This package was not part of the preregistered check, so \texttt{paper/data/trivial.csv} carries no row for it.
\section{Limitations and what is not claimed}
The package documents its own limit:
% quote: benchmark-payment-delegation/README.md#L86
\begin{quote}
Keyword-based merchant traps are simplified versus real payment
networks. The mock adapter uses per-task scripts; live models may need
more turns. Public tasks may appear in training
corpora\textemdash{}keep a hidden split for final comparisons.
\end{quote}
{\footnotesize Source: \href{https://github.com/pooriaarab/benchmark-payment-delegation/blob/v0.1.0/README.md#L86}{\texttt{benchmark-payment-delegation:README.md\#L86}}.}

This report claims no model capability: it records no real-model run, no leaderboard, and no comparison between models.
These offline numbers describe the graders and the scripted policies. They say nothing about a hosted model.
Package status is \texttt{\pkgStatus{}}; saturation is \texttt{\pkgSaturation{}} (\texttt{paper/data/suite.json}).
Disclosure: the package was built by AI coding agents in sessions the author configured, the reviews cited here
are agent reviews, and this report was generated by \texttt{scripts/pkg-reports.mjs} on \pkgSnapshotDate{} from the cached sources named above.
